issues.description: The total sample combines a nationally representative sample (n=2,500) with a sports-wagering oversample (n=1,500). This means the combined N=4,000 sample is not representative—it is heavily overweighted toward gamblers. Analyses using the full sample (especially those involving gambling) will be systematically biased. The authors do not clearly specify which analyses will use the representative sample alone versus the combined sample, nor do they describe any weighting procedures to account for the oversample.
issues.quote: This work will make use of an upcoming study (N=4,000) involving a representative sample of the U.S. population (n=2,500) and a sample of sports-wagering individuals in the U.S. (n=1,500).

issues.description: Pornography and gambling are assessed with validated, behavior-specific instruments (Brief Pornography Screen and PGSI) in addition to the modified NIDA-ASSIST, whereas all substance use outcomes rely solely on the modified NIDA-ASSIST. This creates a fundamental asymmetry: pornography has the most sensitive, validated measures while substances have unvalidated, modified measures. Any differential findings could be attributable to measurement quality rather than true differences in the role of moral incongruence.
issues.quote: These will be included to allow fully parallel analysis across behaviors and substances (i.e., everything will be on the exact same scale using the exact same measurements). Although such an approach is not currently validated for gambling or pornography, given the inclusion of other validated scales to assess these outcomes (see below), including them within the NIDA-ASSIST will not decrement our ability to evaluate our key hypotheses.

issues.description: The Problem Gambling Severity Index in the supplemental materials uses non-standard response scoring: Never (0), Sometimes (2), Most of the time (4), Almost Always (5). The validated PGSI uses 0, 1, 2, 3 scoring. The values shown are inconsistent even with themselves—if doubling the standard values, 'Almost Always' should be 6, not 5. This scoring error would invalidate the PGSI results and prevent comparison with normative data or prior literature.
issues.quote: Never (0) | Sometimes (2) | Most of the time (4) | Almost Always (5)

issues.description: The Brief Pornography Screen is described in the text as using a 'three-point scale of 0 (never) to 2 (very often)' with summed responses, but the supplemental materials show scoring as Never (0), Occasionally (2), Very Often (4). These are inconsistent—if the actual scoring is 0, 2, 4, the total range would be 0-20, not the 0-10 range expected from the validated instrument. This discrepancy must be resolved as it affects interpretation and comparability with prior studies.
issues.quote: on a three-point scale of 0 (never) to 2 (very often). Responses are summed.

issues.description: The NIDA-ASSIST has been substantially modified: an additional frequency category ('more than once per day') was added, pornography and gambling were added as response options, and the instrument is being used to create composite scores for behaviors it was never designed to assess. None of these modifications have been validated. The psychometric properties of the modified instrument are unknown, making the substance use outcomes of uncertain reliability and validity.
issues.quote: we will modify response options by adding an additional frequency category of more than once per day... We will also include pornography and gambling as response options on the NIDA-ASSIST, in addition to the measures listed above.

issues.description: The NIDA-ASSIST composite averages three items scored 0-5 (frequency-based) with two items scored on a 0-3-6 scale (yes/no-type). Averaging these without standardization gives disproportionate weight to the 0-3-6 items (which have a wider effective range). This creates an unbalanced composite where the two binary-style items could dominate the overall score, distorting the measure of problematic use.
issues.quote: Participants will also respond to two questions... for each substance on 3 point scale (0 = No, Never; 3 = Yes, but not in the past 3 months; and 6 = Yes, In the past 3 months). Responses to each of the above five items will be averaged for each substance of interest

issues.description: The study is substantially underpowered for prescription drug misuse (estimated power = .301) and illicit substances (estimated power = .472-.764). These are recognized addictive disorders central to the study's hypotheses. The fallback analysis (using the lower bound of the pornography CI as the equivalence region) is a much weaker test that cannot evaluate equivalence with null. This means the study cannot adequately test its own hypotheses for two of the seven target behaviors.
issues.quote: in the case of illicit drug use (prevalence estimated at 6%-12% of the population) and prescription drug misuse (prevalence estimated at 3.5% of the population), it is possible, if not probable, that our final sample sizes will fall below the minimum size required to detect effects that small

issues.description: Eight moderation analyses are planned, but no correction for multiple comparisons (e.g., Bonferroni, Holm, or false discovery rate) is described for the primary hypothesis tests. This inflates the family-wise Type I error rate substantially. While bivariate correlations are noted to use Holm-adjusted test statistics, this adjustment is not applied to the focal moderation analyses.
issues.quote: In total, we will conduct 8 moderation analyses for moral disapproval and frequency, corresponding to the 8 target behaviors/variables of interest

issues.description: The study explicitly aims to 'demonstrate' that moral incongruence is unique to sexual behavior rather than to objectively test whether it is. This confirmatory framing, combined with the choice of an 'extremely conservative' SESOI that makes it easier to achieve equivalence for non-pornography behaviors, suggests the study design is structured to confirm the authors' preferred hypothesis rather than to provide a balanced test.
issues.quote: we aim to demonstrate that—consistent with the ICD-11 decision to include moral distress as a diagnostic consideration when applying a diagnosis of CSBD—the role moral incongruence in predicting feelings of dysregulation is unique to sexual behavior, in contrast with other addictions.

issues.subcategory: construct validity of moral disapproval across behaviors
issues.description: Moral disapproval of illicit drugs and prescription drug misuse is likely to show severe ceiling effects (most people morally disapprove), while moral disapproval of alcohol is likely to show floor effects (most people do not morally disapprove). This restricted variance would attenuate interaction effects for these substances, making it appear that moral incongruence is absent when the null finding is actually an artifact of distributional properties. The authors do not discuss or plan to assess this possibility.
issues.quote: we will ask participants to rate their agreement with the following statement 'I believe that using ________ is morally wrong' on a scale of 1 (strongly disagree) to 7 (strongly agree).

issues.description: Different measures assess different time frames: frequency of use covers the past 12 months, the NIDA-ASSIST problem items cover the past 3 months, and the Brief Pornography Screen covers the past 6 months. This temporal misalignment could introduce noise and attenuate associations differentially across behaviors, complicating interpretation and cross-behavior comparisons.
issues.quote: participants will report the frequency with which they have engaged in those behaviors over the past 12 months... In the past three months, how often have you had a strong desire or urge... In the last 6 months, have any of these situations happened to you

issues.subcategory: confounding of moral disapproval with shame/guilt in substance use
issues.description: For substance use disorders, moral disapproval of one's own substance use may be a consequence of addiction severity (people who have experienced more negative consequences may be more likely to view their behavior as morally wrong). This reverse causality or confounding is conceptually distinct from the pornography case, where moral disapproval typically precedes use. The authors do not address how the causal direction of moral disapproval may differ across behavior types.
issues.quote: There is certainly evidence that many individuals with substance use disorders morally disapprove of their own behaviors (Matthews et al., 2017) and that individuals with gambling disorder often view their behaviors to be a moral failure

issues.description: Moral disapproval is measured with a single item for each behavior. Single-item measures have unknown reliability, which cannot be estimated, and may not capture the full construct of moral disapproval. While consistent with prior pornography research, extending this approach to seven different behaviors amplifies the risk of measurement error differentially affecting cross-behavior comparisons.
issues.quote: we will ask participants to rate their agreement with the following statement 'I believe that using ________ is morally wrong' on a scale of 1 (strongly disagree) to 7 (strongly agree).

issues.description: The text describes the key interaction as being between 'moral disapproval of an action with severity of consequences from the action,' but the actual operationalization throughout the rest of the manuscript is moral disapproval × frequency of behavior. This inconsistency creates confusion about what is actually being tested.
issues.quote: Central to the proposed study is the measurement of moral incongruence as the interaction of moral disapproval of an action with severity of consequences from the action.

issues.description: The SESOI (δ=.11) is derived from the smallest effect observed across multiple prior studies that used different measures, different operationalizations of moral incongruence, and different populations. The authors acknowledge that the most parallel prior study found a substantially larger effect (β=.270), yet they use the smallest effect from a non-parallel study as their SESOI. This choice makes equivalence easier to achieve for non-pornography behaviors, systematically favoring the authors' hypothesis.
issues.quote: we elected to set our SESOI (δ) for our equivalence interval equal to the observed standardized estimate (β value) corresponding to the smallest effect listed above (β=.11, ΔR2 = .012, f2 = .016, Cohen's d = .25, Grubbs, Lee, et al., 2020). Notably, this effect was observed for an interaction between religiousness (as opposed to moral disapproval directly) and pornography viewing frequency

issues.subcategory: BPS item 5 confounds moral incongruence with addiction
issues.description: Item 5 of the Brief Pornography Screen ('You continue to use pornography even though you feel guilty about it') directly taps into the experience of using pornography despite moral conflict—which is essentially what moral incongruence predicts. This creates criterion contamination where the predictor (moral incongruence) overlaps conceptually with the criterion measure, artificially inflating the association for pornography relative to other behaviors whose outcome measures lack analogous items.
issues.quote: 5. You continue to use pornography even though you feel guilty about it.

issues.description: The cross-sectional design prevents establishing temporal ordering. For the moral incongruence interaction, it is impossible to determine whether moral disapproval precedes and amplifies the frequency-addiction link, or whether experiencing addiction symptoms leads to both moral disapproval and higher frequency reports. This is acknowledged but is a fundamental limitation for the causal claims implied by the model.
issues.quote: This sample is cross-sectional, which limits the temporal ordering of variables.

issues.description: The authors rely entirely on YouGov's proprietary data quality standards and do not plan any independent attention checks, response validity indicators, or careless responding detection methods. This is insufficient for a study of this scale and importance, particularly given the length of the survey and the sensitivity of the topics.
issues.quote: As this data will be obtained via YouGov Opinion Polling, certain measures of quality control and responsiveness are guaranteed as a part of their data collection process based on their proprietary data collection standards. Accordingly, we do not anticipate having to remove responses from the dataset due to inattentive or invalid response styles

issues.description: The authors assume zero unplanned missingness, which is unrealistic even with panel data. No procedures for handling missing data (e.g., listwise deletion, multiple imputation, full information maximum likelihood) are specified. If any missingness occurs, the pre-registered plan provides no guidance.
issues.quote: Additionally, we anticipate no unplanned missingness of data.

issues.description: Only age, gender, and religiousness are included as covariates. Important potential confounders such as mental health status, socioeconomic status, education, relationship status, and social desirability are not controlled for. Given that these variables are associated with both moral attitudes and addictive behaviors, their omission could bias results.
issues.quote: we intend on including religiousness, age, and gender as covariates, as prior work has demonstrated clear links between such variables and self-reported problematic pornography use

issues.description: The gambling frequency item aggregates vastly different gambling behaviors (casino gambling, lottery tickets, fantasy sports, esports betting, sports betting, cards, online gambling) into a single frequency measure. Someone buying monthly lottery tickets is coded the same as someone betting monthly at a casino, despite very different risk profiles and moral salience. This heterogeneity may introduce substantial measurement error.
issues.quote: gambling refers to any recreational activity in which money or something of value is wagered, bet, or risked for the potential of winning more money. Examples of these types of activities include: gambling in casinos or online, buying lottery tickets, playing fantasy sports for money, placing bets on esports

issues.description: The Anderson-Hauck equivalence test for regression requires specifying an equivalence region, but the chosen region (δ=|.11|) is based on a standardized beta from a study using a different moderator (religiousness vs. moral disapproval) and a different outcome measure. The appropriateness of transplanting this effect size as a meaningful SESOI for entirely different behavioral domains (substance use, gambling) is questionable.
issues.quote: We will use the Anderson-Hauck equivalence test for regression (Counsell & Cribbie, 2015), with an equivalence region based on the smallest effect size of interest (SESOI) of δ= .27.

issues.description: The text states the SESOI is δ=.27 in one location but δ=.11 (|β|=.11) in the detailed justification. These appear to refer to different metrics (Cohen's d vs. standardized beta), but this is not clearly distinguished, creating confusion about the actual equivalence bounds being used.
issues.quote: with an equivalence region based on the smallest effect size of interest (SESOI) of δ= .27... we elected to set our SESOI (δ) for our equivalence interval equal to the observed standardized estimate (β value) corresponding to the smallest effect listed above (β=.11

issues.subcategory: religiousness measured at different time point
issues.description: Religiousness, age, and gender are obtained from YouGov panel data rather than measured at the time of survey completion. Panel data may have been collected at a substantially different time point, introducing potential temporal inconsistency with the other study variables, particularly for religiousness which can change over time.
issues.quote: Age, gender, and religiousness will be assessed using panel data provided by YouGov (i.e., not as a part of our survey).

issues.description: Gender is coded as binary (1=male, 0=not-male), which collapses all non-male gender identities into a single category. This may not adequately capture gender-related variation in moral attitudes or addictive behaviors, and the 'not-male' category could be heterogeneous.
issues.quote: gender (binary where 1 = male, and 0 =not-male)

issues.description: Social desirability is not measured or controlled for, despite being highly relevant to self-reports of morally disapproved behaviors (substance use, pornography use, gambling). Differential social desirability across behaviors could systematically bias both frequency reports and moral disapproval ratings.
issues.quote: we intend on including religiousness, age, and gender as covariates

issues.subcategory: asymmetry in construct meaning across behaviors
issues.description: The meaning of 'moral disapproval' likely differs qualitatively across behaviors. Moral disapproval of pornography often stems from pre-existing religious/cultural values, while moral disapproval of substance use may be a post-hoc consequence of experiencing addiction. Treating these as equivalent constructs across behaviors may be conceptually invalid, and any differential findings could reflect differences in what moral disapproval means rather than differences in the moral incongruence mechanism.
issues.quote: For each substance, we will ask participants to rate their agreement with the following statement 'I believe that using ________ is morally wrong'

issues.description: Many of the variables (frequency scales, moral disapproval, PGSI items, BPS items) are ordinal with few categories (3-7 points). Treating these as continuous in OLS regression may violate assumptions, and interactions of ordinal variables are especially prone to artifacts. While the authors mention checking regression assumptions, they do not specify what alternative methods would be used or what constitutes a 'substantial' violation.
issues.quote: Although Ordinary Least Squares techniques (such as the moderation analyses conducted by the Interactive application) in large sample sizes are often robust against some violations (Schmidt & Finan, 2018), in cases where assumptions are substantially violated, we will conduct supplemental analyses to test the robustness of our models, as appropriate.

issues.description: The study uses data from a larger project designed primarily to assess sports-wagering behaviors. The measures enabling the current hypotheses are added to an existing survey, meaning the authors have limited control over survey length, participant fatigue, question ordering, and other design features that could affect data quality for their specific research questions.
issues.quote: Participants will be recruited in late March of 2022 as a part of a larger study of sports wagering behaviors in the American populace funded by the International Center for Responsible Gaming.

issues.subcategory: sports-wagering oversample not addressed in power analysis
issues.description: The power analysis treats the gambling effective N as the sum of national sample gamblers plus the entire sports-betting oversample (n=3,325). However, the sports-betting oversample is a non-random, self-selected group with different characteristics than the representative sample. Combining these groups without accounting for their different sampling frames may inflate apparent statistical power while introducing systematic bias in effect estimates.
issues.quote: Gambling | 73% (national sample) 100% (sports-betting oversample) | 3,325

issues.description: The manuscript states that only participants who endorse past-year use will complete further measures of problematic use, but also states that 'we will administer measures of problematic use and moral disapproval to all participants in the sample.' These statements appear contradictory, and the actual inclusion/exclusion criteria for each analysis are not clearly specified.
issues.quote: Only participants who endorse past-year use will complete further measures of problematic use... we will administer measures of problematic use and moral disapproval to all participants in the sample.

issues.subcategory: range restriction in substance use frequency
issues.description: For substances with low base rates (prescription drug misuse, illicit drugs), not only are sample sizes small, but there is likely severe range restriction in both frequency and moral disapproval variables. Most users of these substances may use infrequently, and moral disapproval is likely highly skewed. This restriction of range would attenuate interaction effects regardless of whether moral incongruence truly operates for these behaviors.
issues.quote: in the case of illicit drug use (prevalence estimated at 6%-12% of the population) and prescription drug misuse (prevalence estimated at 3.5% of the population)

issues.description: The hypotheses are structured asymmetrically: the authors predict moral incongruence WILL predict pornography addiction (alternative hypothesis requiring significance) but will NOT predict gambling/substance addiction (null hypothesis requiring equivalence testing). This means pornography findings only need to reach significance while other behaviors need to demonstrate equivalence—a much harder standard. This asymmetry makes confirmation of the overall theory more likely even if effect sizes are similar across behaviors.
issues.quote: We expect to find that moral incongruence regarding pornography use will predict self-reported feelings of addiction... We expect to find that moral incongruence as it relates to gambling behaviors, will not predict self-reported levels of gambling disorder symptoms.
